body:
Found on getwyrd/wyrd-pdca (template v0.58.0).

## What happens

`pdca flow <ids>` over a batch whose brief names a dependency that is neither in the batch nor a COMPLETE bundle ends in a Python traceback:

```
  File ".../pdca_harness/cli.py", line 716, in _flow_claimed
  File ".../pdca_harness/flow.py", line 2179, in flow_ids
  File ".../pdca_harness/flow.py", line 1724, in _drive_and_act
  File ".../pdca_harness/waves.py", line 149, in compute_waves
  File ".../pdca_harness/waves.py", line 78, in check_dep_graph
ValueError: issue_736: declared dependency '773' is neither in this batch nor an existing COMPLETE bundle
```

The refusal itself is right — `check_dep_graph` validates before any work, and the message names the bundle and the dependency. The defect is that nothing on the `flow` path catches it, so an operator error reads as a harness crash. The same `ValueError` is raised for a dependency cycle.

It is easy to reach: a split parent's `flow` adopts its children, so `pdca flow <parent>` hits it through a child's dependency the operator never named. The observed case was a prerequisite fixed outside the cycle (tracker issue closed by an unrelated PR), whose bundle therefore never reached COMPLETE.

## Fix

Raise a dedicated `DependencyGraphError(ValueError)` from `check_dep_graph` and catch it in `cli._flow`: print the message plus the ways out (add the prerequisite to the batch, drop the edge from the brief when the prerequisite landed outside the cycle, or finish it first), exit 2 — the same shape `Config.load`'s errors already get (#92). Subclassing `ValueError` keeps every existing caller and test that expects `ValueError` working.
title: flow: an unresolvable dependency crashes with a traceback instead of a one-line refusal
